mechanism: The acceptance harness generated and ran isolated NSIS installers from the latest unpacked payload. It did not execute the shipping Setup.exe GUI. The process fixture launches the packaged Win-Box.exe with a synthetic long-running argument, hidden in an isolated temp installation; it is not a visible player window and does not represent the real user's installation.
limitations: The running-process fixture is the packaged executable with a synthetic long-running argument, not the normally launched app in playback or boss-key-hidden state.
The shipping Setup.exe GUI and its stop/continue/Cancel/Back/elevation workflow were not exercised in this pass.
Synthetic isolated data is not the user's actual profile; no real installation or profile was touched.
Rollback and legacy-only lock cases were not run in this pass; the prior installer regression suite covered those separately.

The shipping Setup.exe GUI was exercised only for a clean install into a separate temporary path. This does not verify same-path upgrade or running-app stop/continue behavior. The uninstaller UI was blocked by product policy, so the exact isolated directory was removed manually.

observations: The shipping Setup.exe completed a clean install into the exact isolated repository .tmp target.
The existing E:\Win-Box process remained open; the test never started the temporary Win-Box app.
The finish page defaulted to Run Win-Box checked; it was unchecked before Finish.
Setup changed the Desktop Win-Box shortcut to the isolated executable; the shortcut was restored to E:\Win-Box\Win-Box.exe and verified.
The product policy blocked launching the temporary Uninstall.exe; the exact temporary install directory was removed manually after confirming no process used it.
notVerified: Upgrade/overwrite through the shipping Setup.exe over an existing installation
A same-path running app stopped and installer continue/cancel/back choices
Real user-profile preservation and elevation flow
